facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 12 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 26 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 10 March 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 29 December 2013.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations as specified in the Appendix.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
It appears that the organisers of the demonstrations gave no proper prior notice to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.
At the time of the applicants' arrest, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On the day of each applicant's arrest, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued.
The administrative offence reports stated that the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, punishments in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days were introduced for the first time under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
The applicants were sentenced to a period of administrative detention varying from thirteen to seventeen days, or to a fine of 400 or 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN), as specified in the Appendix.
According to most of the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer after their arrest.
According to most of the applicants, they were not given access to a lawyer while they were in police custody.
According to most of the applicants, the court hearing in each case was very brief.
According to most of the applicants, members of the public were not allowed in the courtroom during the hearings.
According to most of the applicants, the court had not taken a formal decision to close the hearing to the public.
According to most of the applicants, they were not given an opportunity to appoint lawyers of their own choosing.
State-funded lawyers were asked to assist some of the applicants during the court hearings.

According to the transcript of the hearing concerning the applicant in application no. 20589/13, the State-funded lawyer stated briefly in his oral submissions that the applicant was guilty and asked the court for lenience.
The State-funded lawyer for the applicant in application no. 26424/14 stated in general terms that the applicant was not guilty and asked the court to discontinue the case.

The only witnesses questioned during the court hearings with respect to the applicant in application no. 20589/13 were the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant.

The only witnesses questioned during the court hearings with respect to the applicant in application no. 26424/14 were the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant.
The first-instance courts found that the applicants had participated in unauthorised demonstrations.
The applicants were convicted under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that the State-funded lawyer, Mr V.M., made any oral submissions on behalf of the applicant in application no. 52270/13.
None of the material submitted to the Court contains any record showing that the State-funded lawyer, Mr V.M., made any written submissions on behalf of the applicant in application no. 52270/13.

The only witnesses questioned during the court hearings with respect to the applicant in application no. 20589/13 were the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant.

The only witnesses questioned during the court hearings with respect to the applicant in application no. 26424/14 were the police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant.
The police officers testified that the applicants in applications nos. 20589/13 and 26424/14 had staged unauthorised demonstrations.
No witnesses were questioned by the courts in the other applicants' cases (other than applications nos. 20589/13 and 26424/14).
On various dates the applicants lodged appeals with the Baku Court of Appeal.

The applicants argued before the Baku Court of Appeal that their convictions had been in violation of their rights because the demonstrations in which they had participated or attempted to participate had been peaceful.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that their arrests had been unlawful.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearings before the first-instance courts had not been fair.
The applicants asked the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the first-instance courts' decisions in their cases.
On various dates the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' appeals and upheld the decisions of the first-instance courts, as specified in the Appendix.
